title: Whether Jelly Roll could read music
summary: Clem says Jelly could read and play theater shows, but liked playing only his own numbers.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: So... Did Jelly read pretty well when you knew him?

Yes, he could. But he was great for showing off. Well, during his time out here, he was the best piano player. So he didn't fool with no popular numbers. But everything he played with his own numbers, he could give it a name or something. But he could read, yeah. Because when I remember going to a theater, everybody had to read because they had to play. What they call... Some of it was a transcription. And the other was a stock music. So we had to use it for the show. Yeah, he could read.
In Los Angeles, a theater, a diamond.

I don't know if you couldn't read nothing, though. Mm-hmm. Like he spoke about the show. I don't know if you couldn't read nothing. When I just show him, his cause of wine, boy, don't deny my name. That's right. And I'm glad to hear you say that because it's all funny about him being any good reader. He's never no good reader. He criticized his teachers wrongly, too. I was surprised. Yeah, when he made all them trips that got on his feet, composed the numbers. I said, well, he's pretty great. He turned it pretty quick. Well, that's why I thought he stole this number from Joe Oliver, King Porter Stomp. Because I heard Oliver play it. He played it, but I never seen it in music before because it didn't have this Wolverine in music. Everything was jelly roll, jelly roll. That's my number. That's my number. That's how he would... People didn't want to play nothing but his numbers. He'd go to another cafe or cabaret to hear other popular numbers. Just come there to hear and play his numbers.
